related_questions.question: What vaccines need boosters as adults?

text_blocks.snippet: Several vaccines require booster shots for adults to maintain long-term protection. These include vaccines for tetanus, diphtheria, and pertussis (Tdap or Td), measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR), and potentially pneumococcal and meningococcal depending on individual risk factors. Additionally, influenza (flu) vaccines are recommended annually. COVID-19 vaccines also require boosters.
snippet_highlighted_words: tetanus, diphtheria, and pertussis (Tdap or Td), measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR), and potentially pneumococcal and meningococcal

list.snippet: Tetanus, Diphtheria, and Pertussis (Tdap/Td): A Tdap booster is recommended every 10 years for adults. Pregnant women should receive a Tdap booster during each pregnancy.
Influenza (Flu): The flu vaccine is recommended annually for all adults 6 months and older.
COVID-19: Boosters are recommended for maintaining protection against COVID-19, though the specific recommendations may change based on circulating variants and individual risk factors.

text_blocks.snippet: Vaccines That May Require Boosters or Additional Doses:

list.title: Measles, Mumps, and Rubella (MMR):
list.snippet: Adults born in 1957 or later should ideally have two doses of the MMR vaccine. If you were born before 1957, you might have already had natural infections and only need one dose.

list.title: Hepatitis B:
list.snippet: Recommended for adults up to age 59, and some older adults with risk factors, may require boosters.

list.title: Pneumococcal:
list.snippet: While a single dose may be sufficient for some adults, those with certain risk factors or at 65 and older may need a booster or additional dose.

list.title: Meningococcal:
list.snippet: A booster may be needed if it has been at least 4 years since the last dose and if the individual has a high risk of infection, according to Drugs.com.

list.title: Shingles (Shingrix):
list.snippet: Recommended for adults 50 and older, given in two doses.

list.title: HPV:
list.snippet: Recommended for adults up to 26 years old, and some adults aged 27 through 45, according to the CDC.

list.title: Individual Risk Factors:
list.snippet: Your medical history, lifestyle, and occupation can influence which vaccines you need and how often you need them.

list.title: Consult a Healthcare Professional:
list.snippet: It's always best to discuss your vaccination needs with your doctor or other healthcare provider to ensure you're up-to-date on all recommended vaccines, according to the County of San Diego.
